newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway says won't privatise telecoms company.
newsitem.headline: Norway says won't privatise telecoms company.

text.p: The Norwegian government is not going to privatise, wholly or partly, state-owned telecommunications group Telenor, a spokesman for the Transport and Communications Ministry said on Wednesday.
"There are no plans to list Telenor on the stock exchange," the spokesman said.

He was commenting on remarks by Telenor Managing Director Tormod Hermansen, who told financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv on Tuesday that he could see Telenor listed on the Oslo Bourse as well as on stock exchanges abroad.
Hermansen was quoted as saying he would ask the government this year to raise between five to six billion crowns in investment capital for Telenor through two share issues.

Dagens Naeringsliv on Wednesday quoted Transport and Communications Minister Sissel Roenbeck as saying the government would remain sole owner of Telenor. But the report said her ministry was now ordering estimates on the value of the company in what could be a preparation for a partial privatisation.
The ministry spokesman confirmed estimates were being made, but explained: "An estimate of the company's value is good to have when Telenor borrows money on the international market."
